# Frozen-runner branch fixtures

Generated by `../make_branch_fixtures.R` and `../make_timed_failure.R`. Both evaluate the setup portion of the existing `code/bench_v2/tests/run_local_runner.R` wrapper in memory, then call the frozen runner's `main` on three local synthetic inputs. They use the wrapper's documented local glmnet 4.1-10 compatibility shim; this is not production glmnet 5.1 or a benchmark. Frozen runner source SHA-256: `3e01c77b27ad96ad8ec4761b6b25ea5511d357e8aa08a1db7b2972e71734f42c`.

- `inputs/p0005/` and `inputs_manifest.csv` hold the three p=5, n=200 inputs and their exact component/file hashes and seeds. The null case has fold-opposed response components; the singleton case has one orthogonal signal column; the failed case uses the singleton response with a non-centred first design column.
- `results/branch_fixture/` contains the original three outputs, each written by frozen `main` as RDS/CSV/SHA-256/done. Null has zero kept predictors, singleton has one, and all six failure rows have NA coefficients.
- The original failure completes so quickly on Windows that its `runtime_s` is zero; the frozen validator correctly refuses that record under its positive-runtime rule. It is retained for audit.
- `results/branch_failure/` contains a second runner-written failure record from the same input. Its test wrapper inserts only a 50-ms scheduling delay immediately before calling the unchanged frozen `assert_inputs`; this obtains a measurable elapsed time without changing the underlying failure, fitting source, or evidence. The record is not an independent timing measurement. The frozen validator's all-NA `k` column requires a wrapper type normalization because CSV inference otherwise changes integer NA to logical NA.
- `../test_branch_fixtures.R` validates the null, singleton and delayed failure outputs as complete saved records, then verifies two semantic corruptions per record through both the shared object and file validator. Temporary corruptions are rehashed and deleted after the test; the original records remain unchanged.
